title: Data Literacy for Public Decisions
learners: Adult learners with spreadsheet familiarity but no assumed statistics course.
coursePurpose: Interpret tables, rates, uncertainty, and visual claims well enough to critique a public-facing data argument.
outcomes: Calculate and interpret a rate with an appropriate denominator.
Identify a misleading visual encoding and explain its effect.
Write a bounded evidence claim that distinguishes association from causation.

sourcePacket.content: District A: 40 incidents among 2,000 riders. District B: 30 incidents among 1,000 riders. Counts and rates support different rankings.
No variable in the packet establishes why the districts differ; causal explanations are unsupported.
A copied worksheet header calls the incident values percentages, but the rows contain whole-number counts and separate rider denominators. The header is unreliable and must be reconciled before use.
A margin note says District A has the higher incident rate. The supplied counts and denominators instead calculate to 2% for District A and 3% for District B.

localConstraints: Do not add demographic explanations absent from the packet.
adversarialConditions: A raw count invites the opposite ranking from the rate.
The source contains no causal evidence.
A mislabeled header and a contradictory narrative must not override the computable record.
